reason: Dev-only error overlay rendering framework-generated error payload (highlightedCode produced by the build tool's own highlighter) inside a shadow root; no attacker-controlled input reaches the innerHTML sinks in a realistic threat model.
exec() builds the git pull command only from the ROOT constant with no user-controlled input, so there is no code/command injection vector for CWE-94 in the shown code.
Unit test fixtures with dummy passwords and a sample bcrypt hash used to test isHashedPassword; these are not real credentials granting access to anything, so CWE-798 does not apply.

The flagged innerHTML assignment is on a detached div inside a stripScripts sanitization helper in frontend form-summary code; no untrusted taint flow or dangerous DOM insertion of its output is shown, so the sink form alone does not make it exploitable.

Cache read() derives the filename via generateFileLocation() from an internal cache key set by application code, with no evidence of user-controlled path components, so path traversal is not demonstrated.
Demo/sample script where the file path comes from the helper's getTemporaryFilename() and hardcoded template paths, with no external input, so there is no path traversal.
path.join is used to build client-side URL strings from the internal baseHRef and hardcoded route constants like '/api/v1', not filesystem paths from user input, so CWE-22 is inapplicable.

Although $id_dependente is interpolated into the SQL string, it is trimmed and strictly validated with is_numeric() with a 400 exit otherwise, which blocks injection payloads; parameterization would be cleaner but the finding is not exploitable.
Pickle is used only to persist and reload the library's own local object-node mapping from a developer-specified persist_dir (trusted local storage), not to deserialize untrusted external data.

shell_exec of rrdtool restore in an admin CLI maintenance script makes no server-side HTTP request, so CWE-918 (SSRF) is inapplicable, and the file arguments come from operator-controlled CLI context rather than untrusted remote input.
